research_rejections.title: Dead-End Job
research_rejections.reason: Netflix identifies this as a contemporary workplace-horror limited series. Across its episodes, the central structure is a sequence of dangerous paid shifts and supernatural encounters rather than a sustained invented fantasy world, kingdom/faction politics, or a developed magic system. The Korea Times' creator interview and Cineplay's whole-season assessment corroborate its horror-anthology structure and satirical labor focus. Not a sufficiently strong fit for the mature high-fantasy worldbuilding baseline.

research_rejections.title: Remarkably Bright Creatures
research_rejections.reason: Netflix's synopsis and the Associated Press review describe a present-day aquarium-set emotional drama about grief, family and friendship with an unusually perceptive octopus. It has no substantive invented fantasy setting, magic system, mythic factions or fantasy adventure; creature-related wording is a misleading search match.
